next_state_election.name: General Election
next_state_election.source_name: Utah Lieutenant Governor's Office — Current Election Information

glance_notes.source_name: Utah Lieutenant Governor's Office — 2026 Utah Election Calendar
glance_notes.text: 2026 General Election Registration Deadline: Utah's regular voter registration deadline for the November 3, 2026 General Election is October 23 at 5:00 p.m. A voter who misses that deadline may still register and vote provisionally at an early-voting location or on Election Day.

glance_notes.source_name: Utah Lieutenant Governor's Office — Register to Vote
glance_notes.text: Same-Day Registration Available: Utah provides same-day voter registration. An otherwise eligible person who misses the regular registration deadline may register and cast a provisional ballot during qualifying early voting or at a voting location on Election Day. Identification requirements apply.

glance_notes.source_name: Utah Lieutenant Governor's Office — 2026 Utah Election Calendar
glance_notes.text: Mail Ballots Begin October 13: For the November 3, 2026 General Election, October 13 is the first day election officials may send mail ballots to active registered voters. Utah's 2026 election materials state that active registered voters receive a ballot in the mail automatically.

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: Eligible Utah residents may register online, by mail or email, or in person at their county clerk's office. To register, a person must be a U.S. citizen, have been a Utah resident for at least 30 days immediately before the election and meet the applicable age requirement. A person who will be 18 on or before the General Election may be eligible to participate under Utah's preregistration and primary-election rules. Utah also provides same-day registration through the provisional-ballot process for otherwise eligible voters who miss the regular registration deadline.
register.glance_value: Online, mail, email, in person and same-day registration
register.source_name: Utah Lieutenant Governor's Office — Learn How to Register to Vote
register.internal_note: Utah's official voter guidance confirms online registration at voter.utah.gov, paper registration by mail or email and in-person registration through county clerks. Utah requires 30 days of state residency before the election. Utah Code 20A-2-102.5 provides registration through a provisional ballot during early voting or on Election Day after the ordinary deadline.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Use Utah's official voter registration portal to check your registration status, update voter information and manage voter-specific election information. Voters should confirm that their residential and mailing addresses are current so election officials can send the correct ballot. Questions about an individual voter record should be directed to the voter's county clerk.
check_registration.glance_value: Check through Utah's Voter Registration Portal
check_registration.source_name: Utah Lieutenant Governor's Office — Utah Voter Information
check_registration.internal_note: Vote.Utah.gov provides the state's Voter Registration Portal as well as ballot tracking, district information and county election contacts.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: For the November 3, 2026 General Election, Utah's regular voter registration deadline is Friday, October 23 at 5:00 p.m. The regular deadline is 11 calendar days before Election Day. A voter who misses that deadline may still register and vote by casting a provisional ballot at an eligible early-voting location or on Election Day. A same-day registrant must satisfy Utah's identification requirements.
deadlines.glance_value: October 23 at 5:00 p.m.; same-day registration available
deadlines.source_name: Utah Lieutenant Governor's Office — 2026 Utah Election Calendar
deadlines.internal_note: The 2026 official calendar expressly labels October 23 as the last day to register and not have to vote a provisional ballot. Utah Code 20A-2-102.5 sets the ordinary deadline at 5:00 p.m. 11 calendar days before the election and separately permits registration through provisional voting during early voting or before polls close on Election Day.

polling_place.label: Find a Voting Location
polling_place.content: Utah uses voting locations and vote centers administered by county clerks. Voters should use Vote.Utah.gov or contact their county clerk to find Election Day voting locations, early-voting locations and ballot drop boxes. Location availability and hours vary by county, so voters should confirm current information shortly before voting.
polling_place.glance_value: Find voting locations through Vote.Utah.gov or your county clerk
polling_place.source_name: Utah Lieutenant Governor's Office — Utah Voter Information
polling_place.internal_note: Utah election administration is county-based. Avoid describing every Utah voting location as a traditional assigned precinct polling place. County clerks publish their specific vote centers, early-voting sites and drop boxes.

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: Utah's General Election is Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Election Day voting locations are open until 8:00 p.m. Mountain Time. Eligible voters who missed the regular registration deadline may register and vote on Election Day by casting a provisional ballot and satisfying Utah's identification requirements. Registered voters voting in person must provide either one qualifying primary form of identification or two qualifying forms that together establish the voter's name and current residence.
election_day.glance_value: Election Day ends at 8:00 p.m. Mountain Time
election_day.source_name: Utah Lieutenant Governor's Office — 2026 Utah Election Calendar
election_day.internal_note: Utah's same-day registration process uses a provisional ballot. Utah's ordinary registered-voter ID rule allows either one qualifying primary ID or two qualifying secondary IDs. A person registering through a provisional ballot has additional identity and residence verification requirements.

polling_hours.label: Voting Location Hours
polling_hours.content: Utah Election Day voting locations close at 8:00 p.m. Mountain Time. Opening times and the specific locations available to voters are administered locally and should be confirmed through Vote.Utah.gov or the voter's county clerk before Election Day.
polling_hours.glance_value: Close at 8:00 p.m. Mountain Time; check county opening hours
polling_hours.source_name: Utah Lieutenant Governor's Office — 2026 Utah Election Calendar
polling_hours.internal_note: Do not invent a uniform statewide opening time without county-specific verification. Utah's election administration is decentralized through county clerks. The statewide Election Day cutoff is 8:00 p.m. Mountain Time.

early_voting.label: Early In-Person Voting
early_voting.content: Utah provides in-person early voting before the General Election. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the early-voting period may begin October 20. State law allows the period to begin 14 days before Election Day and requires counties conducting a reduced schedule to provide at least four early-voting days. The standard period ends Friday, October 30, although an election officer may extend early voting through Monday, November 2. Locations, dates and hours vary by county. Eligible voters who missed the regular registration deadline may register and vote provisionally at an early-voting location.
early_voting.glance_value: Can begin October 20; standard end October 30
early_voting.source_name: Utah Lieutenant Governor's Office — 2026 Utah Election Calendar
early_voting.internal_note: Utah's calendar says early voting can begin October 20 and directs voters to county clerks for specific dates. Utah Code 20A-3a-601 establishes a period beginning 14 days before the election and normally continuing through the Friday before a Tuesday election. County election officers may reduce the schedule to at least four days or extend it through the day before Election Day under applicable law. Do not imply every county necessarily operates every day from October 20-30.

absentee_mail.label: Vote by Mail
absentee_mail.content: Utah uses vote by mail for statewide elections. Active registered voters receive a ballot in the mail automatically. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, October 13 is the first day regular mail ballots may be sent to active registered voters. A voter who needs a ballot mailed to an alternate address or otherwise needs to request a ballot must meet the applicable request deadline; for the 2026 General Election, the final request date is October 27. Completed ballots may be returned by mail, at an authorized ballot drop box or through other county-approved return options. Ballots deposited in a drop box must be returned before 8:00 p.m. on Election Day.
absentee_mail.glance_value: Mail ballots begin October 13; ballot request deadline October 27
absentee_mail.source_name: Utah Lieutenant Governor's Office — 2026 Utah Election Calendar
absentee_mail.flagged_reason: Utah has changed mail-ballot return rules in recent election cycles. The 2026 calendar confirms ballot mailing and request dates, but voters returning a ballot through USPS should follow the current instructions printed with their 2026 ballot or their county clerk's current guidance rather than relying on older postmark guidance.
absentee_mail.internal_note: The official 2026 calendar confirms October 13 as the first day mail ballots can be sent and October 27 as the final ordinary ballot-request date. Vote.Utah.gov confirms drop boxes require return before 8:00 p.m. Election Day. Because Utah mail-ballot receipt/postmark law has been the subject of recent legislative changes, avoid inserting an unverified 2024/2025 postal deadline into the 2026 record. Reverify the precise USPS return rule against current 2026 Utah Code and General Election voter instructions before publication.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: A registered Utah voter voting in person must provide either one qualifying primary form of identification or two qualifying forms that, when combined, establish the voter's name and current residence. Primary identification includes a valid Utah driver license, qualifying Utah or U.S. government photo identification, a Utah concealed-carry permit, a U.S. passport, qualifying tribal identification or a current U.S. military identification card. The two-document option includes several types of government, financial, employment, school and residency records. A voter registering through a provisional ballot must provide identification establishing identity and residence under Utah's same-day registration rules.
voter_id.glance_value: One primary ID or two qualifying secondary IDs
voter_id.source_name: Utah Lieutenant Governor's Office — Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.internal_note: The official Utah ID page states that an already registered voter may present one valid primary ID bearing name and generally a photograph, with tribal ID specifically not requiring a photograph, OR two qualifying forms establishing name and current residence. Utah-issued school IDs from colleges, universities, technical schools or professional schools appear among the secondary-ID options.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: Utah provides multiple voting options for voters with disabilities. Voting locations provide accessible voting equipment with accommodations for voters with visual or hearing impairments. A voter who needs assistance may ask a poll worker or choose another person to assist, except the voter's employer, a trade union representative or a candidate. Utah also permits eligible voters with disabilities to request electronic ballot delivery and return through procedures administered by the county clerk. Vote-by-mail options are also available.
accessible_voting.glance_value: Accessible equipment, assistance and electronic ballot options
accessible_voting.source_name: Utah Lieutenant Governor's Office — Information for Voters with Disabilities
accessible_voting.flagged_reason: The state's accessibility page still contains some election-specific examples dated 2024. The underlying accessibility options remain stated by the current official site, but election-specific deadlines should be obtained from 2026 materials or the county clerk.
accessible_voting.internal_note: The current official page confirms accessible machines, voter-assistance rules and that Utah law permits voters with disabilities to send and receive ballots by email. However, the page contains stale 2024 date examples. Therefore retain the general verified accessibility rules but do not reuse the old dates. County clerks should control 2026 electronic-ballot application and return instructions.

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: Utah provides special voting procedures for eligible active-duty military members, qualifying spouses and dependents, and U.S. citizens living outside the United States. Covered voters may request a ballot online or submit the appropriate form to their county clerk and may request delivery by mail, email or fax. Electronic delivery requires the voter to waive ballot secrecy under Utah law. Utah also permits qualifying military and overseas voters to return ballots electronically by email or fax under its special procedures, which likewise require waiver of ballot secrecy. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, ballots are scheduled to be sent to military and overseas voters beginning September 18. The Federal Write-In Absentee Ballot is available when applicable.
military_overseas.glance_value: Ballots sent beginning September 18; electronic delivery and return available
military_overseas.source_name: Utah Lieutenant Governor's Office — Military and Overseas Voters
military_overseas.flagged_reason: The current Utah military and overseas voter webpage contains deadline examples from the 2025 election. The general UOCAVA procedures are current, while 2026 dates must come from the official 2026 election calendar and current county instructions.
military_overseas.internal_note: The official UOCAVA page confirms online/paper requests, mail/email/fax ballot delivery, email/fax ballot return and the secrecy-waiver consequence. The 2026 Candidate Manual confirms September 18, 2026 as the date General Election ballots are sent to military and out-of-country voters. Do not copy the November 3, 2025 application deadline displayed on the current UOCAVA webpage into the 2026 record. Reverify the exact 2026 UOCAVA request and return deadlines closer to Election Day.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: College students may register in Utah if they meet the state's eligibility and residency requirements, including Utah's 30-day residency requirement before the election. Students should use the residence they consider their voting residence and may vote in only one jurisdiction for an election. Students who move should keep both their voter registration and ballot mailing address current. A currently valid identification card issued by a college, university, technical school or professional school in Utah may be used as one of the two secondary identification documents permitted for in-person voting.
student_voting.glance_value: Utah school ID may qualify as one of two secondary IDs
student_voting.source_name: Utah Lieutenant Governor's Office — Voter ID Requirements
student_voting.internal_note: Utah's official voter-ID guidance expressly includes a currently valid ID issued by a college, university, technical school or professional school within Utah among the secondary ID documents. Do not imply that a student ID alone satisfies the ordinary registered-voter ID requirement; it is one of two documents under the secondary-ID route.

sample_ballot.label: Official Ballot Information
sample_ballot.content: Utah voters can use Vote.Utah.gov to obtain voter-specific election information, including information about candidates, issues and voting districts. Ballot contents depend on the voter's residence and political districts, so voters should use their own voter information and county election resources to review the contests that apply to them for the November 3, 2026 General Election.
sample_ballot.glance_value: Use Vote.Utah.gov for voter-specific ballot information
sample_ballot.source_name: Utah Lieutenant Governor's Office — Utah Voter Information
sample_ballot.internal_note: Vote.Utah.gov provides candidate and issue information, district lookup and voter tools. Ballot contents vary by residence. Reverify after final 2026 General Election ballots and voter-information materials are published.

contact.label: Contact the State Election Authority
contact.content: Utah elections are overseen statewide by the Office of the Lieutenant Governor, with county clerks administering elections locally. General election assistance is available from the Lieutenant Governor's Office at 801-538-1041. Voters should contact their county clerk for voter-specific registration, ballot, early-voting, voting-location and ballot-tracking questions.
contact.source_name: Utah Lieutenant Governor's Office — Additional Resources for Voters
contact.internal_note: The current Vote.Utah.gov voter resources page lists 801-538-1041 for the Lieutenant Governor's Office. County clerk contact information is maintained at [https://vote.utah.gov/contact-your-county-election-officials/](https://vote.utah.gov/contact-your-county-election-officials/). No email address was inserted into reader-facing content without a need to do so.

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Use Vote.Utah.gov and your county clerk for official Utah election information. State resources provide voter registration, registration status, ballot tracking, voting locations, candidate and issue information, voter identification requirements, vote-by-mail guidance, accessibility information and military and overseas voting resources. County clerks administer voter registration, mail ballots, early voting, Election Day voting locations, drop boxes and other local election functions.
